decision.rationale: Three blocking defects let LP-04 claim success without authoritative client or resource proof and mishandle the documented in-progress recovery response. Exact-head CI is green, but it does not exercise these counterexamples; the PR is also still draft.

summary: PR #6 adds the LP-04 Skill, deterministic real-HTTP demo, recovery journal, client evidence, facilitator and browser proof. Three exact-head counterexamples block approval: fabricated client evidence passes, child resources are not publicly re-read before COMMITTED/PASS, and IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS becomes terminal REJECTED instead of being retried.

findings.title: Client evidence verifier accepts fabricated execution proof
findings.observation: After format checks, the verifier never consumes rawTranscriptSha256 or requestIds. It only proves the named Skill tree and that caller-supplied Idea/project/report IDs are currently readable and synthetic; objectiveChecks and client metadata remain self-asserted.
findings.trigger: A hand-written record supplies any 64-hex transcript digest, any syntactically valid request ID, PASS objective checks and the ID of any readable synthetic resource.
findings.impact: The command returns PASS and committed documentation can state that Codex or Claude actually executed even when no client session, transcript or request/resource correlation exists, directly defeating AC-15 and the approved plan's no-static-substitution gate.

evidence.description: An exact-head counterexample used clientVersion invented-client, observer hand-written, a zero transcript digest, an unrelated request ID and an invented check; a fake public Idea read was sufficient for verifyClientEvidence to return accepted=true.
requestIds and rawTranscriptSha256 are validated only for shape and then returned; the live loop starts from resourceRefs and never correlates audit/request metadata.
AC-15 requires actual Codex and Claude execution; the approved plan says a hand-written assertion without live request/resource correlation cannot become PASS.
The unit test itself constructs a record in memory and only proves its self-digest; npm verify does not run demo:lp04:verify-client for either committed proof.

findings.remediation: Make PASS depend on independently checkable execution evidence: bind the transcript digest to an actual supplied ignored transcript during generation/verification, correlate every recorded request ID to the claimed resources via authoritative audit/history data, require expected objective check IDs, and include both committed proof validations in the exact-head gate or keep AC-15 explicitly failed.
findings.verification: Add negative tests showing absent/mismatched transcript, unrelated request IDs, arbitrary objective checks and a readable unrelated synthetic resource all fail; both real Codex and Claude records then pass the exact-head validator.

findings.title: Child-resource writes are committed without matching public reads
findings.observation: publicVerify builds checks only for reference names ending in IdeaId or ProjectId. Evidence, progress, attention, conclusion and report IDs are ignored; report-only refs cause zero GETs, while project-bearing writes only prove that the project exists, not that the returned child ID is authoritative. The caller then persists COMMITTED and verifyRun repeats the same omission.
findings.trigger: Any normal or recovered child-resource write returns 2xx, especially report submission whose responseRefs contains only a ReportId, or a later rerun encounters a COMMITTED child entry.
findings.impact: The journal and result can report COMMITTED/VERIFIED/PASS even though the exact evidence, fact, item, conclusion or report was never publicly reconciled. This invalidates the recovery authority and real-HTTP demo evidence required by AC-9/12.

evidence.description: Calling exact-head publicVerify with only activeReportId completed successfully with childVerifyReadCount=0.
step and recoverPending call publicVerify before resolveExecutedEntry, but the verifier discards all child IDs; verifyRun likewise only reads IdeaId and ProjectId refs.
The approved design requires a matching public read before success and requires COMMITTED entries to re-read recorded resources before skipping the write.

findings.remediation: Associate every journaled child ID with its project and authoritative collection/current-report endpoint, then require the exact child ID to appear in a bounded public read before COMMITTED, on terminal skip, and in verifyRun. Do not emit PASS assertions unconditionally when those reads have not succeeded.
findings.verification: Add normal and crash/restart cases for report plus at least one execution child; make a missing/mismatched child fail before COMMITTED and prove terminal reruns perform zero writes but matching public reads.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS is persisted as terminal rejection
findings.observation: Recovery treats every non-2xx response as accepted=false and immediately resolves the journal to REJECTED. It never recognizes IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS, reads retryAfterMs or performs the planned bounded same-body/key retry.
findings.trigger: A restart replays an unresolved write while the original API transaction is still processing and the existing contract returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS.
findings.impact: A temporary and explicitly retryable state becomes permanent local rejection. The next scenario pass sees a terminal mismatch and cannot recover the original intent, violating AC-7 and the Skill's advertised recovery behavior.

evidence.description: An exact-head recovery replay returning 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with retryAfterMs=250 performed one POST and left the journal in REJECTED.
recoverPending and step classify status solely by the 2xx range and resolve all other responses as REJECTED.
The approved design specifies advertised 250 ms waits and at most three exact-body/key retries; the Skill reference promises the same behavior.

findings.remediation: Handle IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS as unresolved: validate and bound retryAfterMs, wait and replay the same frozen entry/key at most the approved limit, and leave an honest unresolved/failed state rather than REJECTED if the limit is exhausted.
findings.verification: Add exact-head tests for in-progress then replay-success and in-progress exhaustion; assert identical body/key, bounded POST count, no changed intent and no premature REJECTED/COMMITTED state.

required_actions.action: Make actual client execution and request/resource correlation independently verifiable, then gate both proof records.
Publicly reconcile each exact child resource before COMMITTED/PASS and on terminal replay.
Implement and test bounded IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS recovery with frozen bytes and key.
